biological.citation: SHANK2 is a frequently amplified oncogene with evolutionarily conserved roles in regulating Hippo signaling. (PMID: 32661924)
biological.summary: SHANK2 (homolog of Drosophila Prosap) was identified in a genome-wide Drosophila screen as a novel regulator of the Hippo pathway. In human cell lines, SHANK2 overexpression deregulates Hippo signaling through competitive binding for a LATS1 activator, promoting cellular transformation and tumor formation in vivo. Depletion of SHANK2 in cancer cell lines with deregulated Hippo pathway restores Hippo signaling and halts proliferation.

biological.citation: SHANK2 establishes auditory hair bundle architecture essential for mammalian hearing. (PMID: 40627398)
biological.summary: SHANK2 localizes to the medial apical surface of developing cochlear hair cells and is regulated by the small GTPase RAP1, independently of known lateral or medial polarity proteins. Hair cell-specific ablation of Shank2 disrupts the V-shaped bundle geometry of outer hair cells, impairs high-frequency amplification, and leads to progressive bundle degeneration and hearing loss. This reveals a non-synaptic role for SHANK2 in establishing stereociliary bundle architecture essential for mammalian hearing.

biological.citation: Autism patient-derived SHANK2B(Y29X) mutation affects the development of ALDH1A1 negative dopamine neuron. (PMID: 38704506)
biological.summary: An autism patient-derived point mutation (SHANK2B Y29X) causes an early stop codon and aberrant splicing that primarily disrupts the SHANK2B isoform. iPSCs carrying this mutation fail to differentiate into functional dopamine neurons, and this defect is rescued by genetic correction. Knock-in mice with the identical mutation exhibit autistic-like behavior, decreased ALDH1A1-negative dopamine neurons, and reduced dopamine release in the ventral tegmental area.
biological.sample_size: iPSC lines from patient and isogenic controls; knock-in mice

biological.citation: SHANK2 mutations impair apoptosis, proliferation and neurite outgrowth during early neuronal differentiation in SH-SY5Y cells. (PMID: 33483523)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated frameshift mutations in SHANK2 in SH-SY5Y cells caused impaired neuronal differentiation marker expression, decreased neurite outgrowth, diminished apoptosis, and increased proliferation. Bi-allelic SHANK2 mutations led to increased p-AKT levels, implicating downstream tyrosine kinase receptor signaling. Additionally, bi-allelic mutant cells showed lower amyloid precursor protein (APP) expression, suggesting a molecular link between SHANK2 and APP.
biological.sample_size: SH-SY5Y cell lines (mono- and bi-allelic mutants)

biological.citation: Inhibitory regulation of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator anion-transporting activities by Shank2. (PMID: 14679199)
biological.summary: Shank2 was shown to physically interact with CFTR via its PDZ domain, as confirmed by yeast two-hybrid assays and co-immunoprecipitation in mammalian cells; mutations in the PDZ domain abolished this interaction. Expression of Shank2 suppressed cAMP-induced phosphorylation and activation of CFTR in NIH 3T3 cells, and stable antisense knockdown of Shank2 in colonic T84 cells strongly increased CFTR currents. These results indicate that Shank2 negatively regulates CFTR-mediated ion transport in epithelial cells.

biological.citation: Shank2 identifies a subset of glycinergic neurons involved in altered nociception in an autism model. (PMID: 37316943)
biological.summary: High levels of Shank2 expression were found to identify a subpopulation of glycinergic inhibitory interneurons in both murine and human dorsal spinal cord. Loss of Shank2 in Shank2-/- mice caused decreased NMDAR levels at excitatory synapses on these inhibitory interneurons and failure to activate glycinergic interneurons during the subacute phase of the formalin pain test. This resulted in increased activation of nociception projection neurons in laminae I and pain hypersensitivity phenotypes.

biological.citation: Downregulation of the Autism Spectrum Disorder Gene Shank2 Decreases Bone Mass in Male Mice. (PMID: 36751416)
biological.summary: Shank2 is expressed in bone and its levels increase during osteoblastogenesis; siRNA knockdown of Shank2 inhibits osteoblastogenesis of primary murine calvarial osteoblasts. Shank2 knockout mice display decreased bone mass due to reduced osteoblastogenesis and bone formation, with unaffected bone resorption. iPSC-derived osteoblasts from a patient with a loss-of-function SHANK2 mutation also showed significantly reduced osteoblast differentiation potential.
biological.sample_size: Shank2-/- mice; primary murine osteoblasts; patient iPSC-derived osteoblasts

biological.citation: Genetic Analysis Implicates Dysregulation of SHANK2 in Renal Cell Carcinoma Progression. (PMID: 36231770)
biological.summary: A genetic association study in 630 RCC patients and controls found that the SHANK2 rs10792565 T allele was significantly associated with increased RCC risk (adjusted OR=1.79, 95% CI=1.32–2.44, p=1.96×10⁻⁴, q=0.030). A pooled analysis of 19 independent studies (1509 RCC vs. 414 normal tissues) showed significantly lower SHANK2 expression in RCC, with low expression correlating with advanced stage and poor prognosis in clear cell and papillary RCC.
biological.sample_size: 630 RCC patients and controls; pooled analysis of 1509 RCC and 414 normal tissues

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - A direct regulatory link between microRNA miR-137 and SHANK2 with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders. (S. Berkel, A. de Sena Cortabitarte, C. Fischer, G.A. Rappold)
biological.summary: In silico analysis identified a putative miR-137 binding site in the SHANK2 3'-UTR; overexpression of miR-137 in SH-SY5Y cells and mouse primary hippocampal neurons significantly lowered endogenous Shank2 protein levels without affecting mRNA, indicating translational repression. Inhibition of miR-137 increased Shank2 protein levels, and comparison of RNA-seq data from schizophrenia dorsolateral prefrontal cortex showed that ~29% of validated miR-137 target genes (including SHANK2) had significant expression differences in schizophrenia patients.
biological.sample_size: SH-SY5Y cells; mouse primary hippocampal neurons; RNA-seq from schizophrenia DLPFC (CommonMind Consortium)

biological.citation: Brain region and gene dosage-differential transcriptomic changes in Shank2-mutant mice. (PMID: 36311025)
biological.summary: RNA-seq transcriptomic analysis of prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and striatum in Shank2 heterozygous and homozygous mutant mice revealed distinct, brain region-specific transcriptomic patterns involving synapse, ribosome, mitochondria, spliceosome, and extracellular matrix gene sets. The prefrontal cortex showed the strongest gene dosage-dependent effects: heterozygous mice displayed increased synaptic gene expression with reverse-ASD patterns, while homozygous mice showed decreased synaptic gene expression with ASD-like patterns. The three brain regions also differed in expression of ASD-related and ASD-risk genes.
biological.sample_size: Shank2 HT and HM mutant mice (adult)
